remediation: R1 — make the terminal branch actually terminal
approvedBy: user (explicit: 'Fix it — exclude FAILED from claim')

defect.title: FAILED is not terminal — outbox processor re-claims permanently-failed rows forever
defect.mechanism: claimBatch selected status IN ('PENDING','FAILED'); markFailed's terminal branch set status='FAILED' without advancing available_at, so available_at stayed permanently <= NOW() and the row satisfied the claim predicate on every tick.

change.commentAdded: Claims PENDING only — retries re-enter via PENDING, so FAILED must stay terminal or rows re-claim forever.

safetyAnalysisBeforeChange.retryPathUnaffected: markFailed's non-terminal branch sets status='PENDING' with a backoff available_at. claimBatch still selects PENDING, so genuine retries are untouched.
safetyAnalysisBeforeChange.staleClaimRecoveryUnaffected: recoverStaleClaims resets expired PROCESSING rows to PENDING, which remains claimable.
safetyAnalysisBeforeChange.operatorReplayUnaffected: replayOutboxEvent (events/core/replay.ts) looks a row up by eventId regardless of status and dispatches directly through the bus. It never depended on claimBatch re-claiming FAILED rows.
safetyAnalysisBeforeChange.dlqUnaffected: The EventOutboxStatus enum contains only PENDING/PROCESSING/PUBLISHED/FAILED — there is no DEAD_LETTERED member. Dead-lettering is a separate table reached via replayDeadLetterById, untouched by this change.
safetyAnalysisBeforeChange.metricsUnaffected: retention.ts counts PENDING/PROCESSING/FAILED for the backlog gauge; that query is independent of the claim predicate.
safetyAnalysisBeforeChange.validationUntouched: The homigo.* namespace check in validation.ts was NOT modified, relaxed, or bypassed.

runtimeVerification.method: The backend runs under `bun --watch`, so it hot-reloaded on the edit. Two read-only 30s observation windows were compared, before and after.

before.interpretation: 1 re-claim per row per 5s tick — storm active

freshEventStillPublishes.conclusion: Normal publishing is unbroken by the claim-predicate change.

testsAdded: every registered event type uses the homigo namespace — iterates EVENT_TYPES and asserts zero offenders
ETA events are registered and pass envelope validation — asserts the three homigo.eta.* types and aggregateType=eta
regressionGuard.guardProvenNonVacuous: The same predicate applied to the pre-fix constant values flags exactly the 3 old ETA entries while passing the 2 valid ones, so the assertion has teeth rather than passing trivially.
regressionGuard.suiteResults: 26 pass / 0 fail across event-foundation, event-bus, event-failure-scenarios, eta-intelligence

notRun.reason: It writes to the live homigo_db, which is a documented hazard in this project. Its coverage of the outbox insert -> claim -> publish path was instead obtained from the fresh-lifecycle run against the real running backend, which is stronger evidence than the in-process test.

testArtifactsLeftInPlace.rows: A small number of PUBLISHED homigo.eta.* outbox rows with synthetic bookingIds were created by the diagnostic scripts.
testArtifactsLeftInPlace.action: LEFT UNTOUCHED — the standing instruction prohibits deleting outbox rows. They are terminal PUBLISHED records and will age out under the normal published-retention policy (EVENTS_OUTBOX_PUBLISHED_RETENTION_DAYS=14).
